label: Q3 2026 (Jul–Sep)
asOf: close of $233.62 on 3 Nov 2026 (MarketBeat); lower after hours
headline: Revenue 2.5x in a year and guidance higher again, yet the stock is half its peak: the market worries about margins and rivals for the chips that switch traffic between GPUs

points.b: Scorpio becomes the largest product line
points.t: The Scorpio X 320-lane GPU-to-GPU switch began shipping in volume; revenue rose 49% q/q and 154% y/y.
From 76% to 72%, with Q4 guided to about 72%: switch chips and board- and module-type hardware are a bigger share and carry lower margins than retimers.

points.b: The stock has halved from its peak
points.t: It closed at $233.62 before the report, against a $483.02 closing high on 30 Jun and a 52-week range of $97.89–499.48; it fell hard in late October with the AI sector.

reaction: Stock: closed at $233.62 (+1.7%, MarketBeat) on report day and fell after hours (Benzinga and Seeking Alpha headlines: results and guidance beat but shares slid); the size of the move and the next-day close are to be added. Consensus from MarketBeat: EPS $1.19, revenue $551M.

segments.title: Where the money comes from and goes
segments.bridgeT: From revenue to non-GAAP operating profit
segments.take: Of every $1 of revenue, about 28 cents is cost of sales and about 28 cents opex, leaving about 45 cents of operating profit. R&D is the biggest expense.

rows.why: The P-Series connects GPUs, CPUs, NICs and storage (PCIe 6); the X-Series handles GPU-to-GPU scale-up, with the 320-lane version in volume this quarter. The company sizes the merchant scale-up switch market at about $20B by 2030.

rows.n: Aries / Taurus signal conditioning and cables
rows.why: Aries retimers carry high-speed signals further over boards and cables; Aries 7 supports PCIe 7 and extends into optics (NPO, LPO). Taurus is an active copper cable module.
Adds memory to CPUs or GPUs over CXL. Paired with Scorpio X, Leo X cuts time-to-first-token for long-context inference by 62% (company testing).

segments.note: The company doesn't disclose revenue by product; it only says Scorpio became the largest line this quarter. Cost of sales is backed out from the 72.4% non-GAAP gross margin.

extras.title: Where it sits in the AI loop
extras.take: Astera Labs makes the wiring that connects chips inside the rack: switch and signal chips between GPU and GPU, GPU and CPU, and chips and memory. Every AI server has several, and more GPUs at higher speeds mean more of them.

items.w: Management's core claim is rising “dollar content per accelerator”: it used to sell only retimers, and now sells switch chips, memory controllers and optical chips too.
NVIDIA links its GPUs with its own NVLink; everyone else (AMD, cloud companies' in-house chips) needs an open alternative, which is Scorpio X's market.
Broadcom has an Ethernet scale-up approach (SUE/ESUN), and Marvell and Credo also make retimers and active cables. Arista launched an Ethernet scale-up architecture this quarter too.
Revenue is concentrated in a few hyperscalers and their custom-chip programs; one program's timing or share can swing a quarter.
Orion is a GPU- and CPU-agnostic full-rack reference design, aimed mainly at neoclouds and enterprises, shipping through OEMs/ODMs from Q1 2027.

extras.title: Where growth comes from
extras.take: Astera's growth comes from how much scale-up networking share Scorpio X wins. Q4 guidance implies annualized revenue near $3B, three times a year ago.

items.w: The Q4 midpoint of $740M is +26% q/q and about +173% y/y. Design wins cover “multiple programs at multiple customers”.
More hardware and switch chips cut gross margin from 76% to 72%. The long-term target is around 70%, so it is still above target.
Non-GAAP opex is growing slower than revenue; Q4 guidance has opex at about $197M, only 22% above this quarter's.
Only next-quarter guidance, with no annual or long-term revenue target.
Customers switching to Ethernet scale-up or in-house links; a big program slipping; gross margin below 70%; inventory still climbing fast.

trends.why: 2.5x in five quarters, +49% q/q in Q3
Down 4 points in a year as hardware mix rises

valuation.take: About 71 times trailing non-GAAP earnings and about 53 times 2026, with a P/S of about 28, below its post-IPO median of about 38 but still among the most expensive chip companies we cover. The price bets on Scorpio X winning the scale-up market.

forward.title: Full-year 2026 from company guidance
forward.note: 2026 revenue about $2.03B (Q4 at the $740M midpoint), about +115% y/y.

scenarios.note: Bear: scale-up shifts to Ethernet or in-house links and revenue stalls at Q4's annualized level; base: Scorpio X wins the main share, about 35% a year for two years; bull: Scorpio, Leo and optical products all ramp. EPS = revenue × non-GAAP operating margin × (1 − 13% tax) ÷ 192M shares. These assumptions are ours and are not forecasts.

pricezone.sub: 2028 EPS × our P/E; price at the 3 Nov close (before the report)
pricezone.why: The price is above the zone: buying at $234, the base case gains about 38% and the bear case loses about 51%, a reward/risk of about 0.7. At the $185 top of the zone the reward/risk is about 1.9; at the $165 low end, about 3.1. The $114 bear price is near the 52-week low of $97.89: this stock's range is wide, and the competitive picture isn't settled.

history.title: Against its own past
history.sub: P/S (TTM revenue, diluted shares), quarter ends; listed in March 2024, so 10 quarter ends from 2024Q2
history.note: About 28x now, below the post-IPO median of about 38x and far below the 74x of end-June. Its P/S has swung between 20x and 74x, a sign of deep disagreement about its long-term share. We calculate it from SEC quarterly revenue, diluted shares and quarter-end closes.

cash.note: Operating cash flow of $341M over the first three quarters trails non-GAAP net income: receivables rose from $83M to $284M and inventory from $59M to $201M, normal in a ramp, but Q4 needs to show them coming back.

insider.title: Effective trades 30 days around the report
insider.text: No effective open-market trades in the 30 days before the report (10/4–11/3). Director Stefan Dyckerhoff sold about $4.7M on 7 Oct under a preset 10b5-1 plan, which doesn't count as effective. Earlier, in August–September, the CEO and other directors made planned or tax-related sales (MarketBeat counts about $127M over three months). The 30 days after the report update daily with Insider Flow; see the Insider Flow page.
